newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX new-look fuel oil market starts trading.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX new-look fuel oil market starts trading.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) launched on Tuesday its new-look fuel oil futures contract.
The new contract was officially launched at 1430 local time in Singapore (0630 GMT). It listed June as the first trading month followed by the subsequent eight months.
The opening June trade was at $98.00 per tonne and was executed by Credit Lyonnais Rouse.
June was quoted at $98.70/$99.00 per tonne a few minutes into trading. Traded volume after five minutes was 60 lots.
Traders have given the contract an optimistic but cautious reaction in the build up to the launch.

They welcomed specification changes that bring the contract more into line with the physical market, but were wary of its potential success given previous contracts for gas oil and crude that failed to receive trade support.
SIMEX has listed a fuel oil contract since 1989, but it has been untraded since 1995 when the specifications of the contract fell out of line with the physical market.

When it was first launched, the SIMEX fuel contract traded a daily average volume of nearly 5,000 lots. But volume dwindled to a mere 162 lots per day in 1995 and since August 1995, the contract has been virtually dormant.
